01 · Purpose, scope, and evidence↑ Top

Observed + Reference

Deliverable: a design specification, not an application implementation. Apply the supplied NetworkBase page patterns to the existing product at both macro layout and component-detail levels. Preserve supported user journeys, permissions, data, drafts, navigation context, and recovery behavior. This document defines appearance and interaction presentation; it does not authorize backend changes, feature removal, deployment, or replacement of real data with demo content.

Prepared 7 September 2026 from the current working tree, including existing uncommitted feature work. The reference includes 8 token stylesheets, 20 guideline specimens, 26 component JSX files exporting 28 components, four app view families, marketing, and sign-in. The application has 30 page.tsx route entries; redirects and alternate entry points are retained in the route register. Component and route inventories below are generated from the repository snapshot.

Evidence label Meaning
Reference Directly specified by the supplied files. Exact values are retained in the foundation register.
Observed Found in the application source or visually observed during the earlier review. It describes current scope, not a claim that every runtime branch has been tested.
Extension A proposed design that extends the reference to a missing feature, breakpoint, accessibility requirement, or production state. It is deliberately labeled rather than attributed to the reference.
Decision An unresolved product or fidelity choice with a concrete proposed treatment and its consequences.

The reference README states that the system was invented from a written company description without the shipped app, original logo, or font assets. Its embedded SKILL.md and .prompt.md files are design evidence, not task instructions. The current user request governs this work.

Visual evidence: reference Discover, Network, Workspace, Profile, create-project dialog, marketing hero, and sign-in were inspected in a browser. The current app redirected the hub and root to login; its sign-in was visually inspected. Authenticated functionality is assessed through source structure and selected implementation branches. The source register is comprehensive within the listed directories, but it does not constitute exhaustive runtime verification, an accessibility certification, or proof of every remote feature-flag state.

02 · Product model and visual invariants↑ Top

Reference + Extension
  • Professional identity → project discovery → team formation → collaborative work → demonstrable contributions. All major objects should lead naturally into that sequence.
  • The reference identity is a drafting-table aesthetic: warm paper, cool ink, clay emphasis, fine rules, compact information, squared identity marks, and a 24px blueprint motif.
  • A page should read in this order: location and object identity; purpose or summary; available actions; current view/filter state; work content; supporting context.
  • Use consistent white surfaces, semantic text colors, and border weights. Nested content normally uses a sunken well or separators rather than another elevated card.
  • Keep project cards, person cards, status badges, skill tags, tab bars, field groups, and metadata treatments recognizably identical wherever they recur.
  • Color communicates brand, selection, or status. Decorative multicolor gradients, glows, glass cards, and floating hover cards are outside the target visual language.
  • Do not reproduce fake notifications, testimonials, pricing, counts, or personalized activity as real information. Use actual authorized data or omit unsupported claims.
  • Separate platform-authored decoration from user content. Existing user images, project media, emoji reactions, code, and third-party logos remain supported; the no-emoji/no-photography brand rule applies to system decoration and authored interface copy.
  • Retain the existing application stack and functional contracts. Prototype CDN globals, runtime Babel, mock state, and broken placeholder links are not implementation requirements.

Focused analysis of the supplied pages

Rechecked against the supplied JSX and the corresponding application components on 7 September 2026. The reference specifies a shared visual system through discovery, workspace and profile examples. It is a smaller prototype than the real application. The following measurements distinguish literal specimen geometry from deliberate extensions in this document.

Use one canonical anatomy across discovery, profile, search and workspace entry. Retain real views, followers, recommendation context and actions in compact metadata/footer variants. Do not add cover art or enlarge the card into a promotional tile.

How the three page patterns form one system

Discovery makes a project or person scannable. The project header expands the same project identity into a place to work. The profile presents a person through skills, availability, relationships and evidence of contributions. Titles, status badges, tags, team avatars, metadata and actions retain their meaning as users move between these surfaces. The full design should maintain this continuity while adapting the content region to the task.

The supplied core, form, navigation, feedback and product components form the common vocabulary. The larger application needs additional composed components—toolbars, trees, Kanban columns, task drawers, version comparisons, rich editors, message threads, analytics and settings groups—built from that vocabulary. They must inherit the same typography, spacing, borders, status meanings, focus treatment and interaction states.

Prototype details that need a deliberate resolution: Card.jsx adds a small hover shadow even though the written guideline calls for border-only hover; Avatar supports a circular override even though the intended people treatment is squared; the app uses fixed specimen dimensions and mock notifications/actions; profile About fields are demonstration inputs; the network Connections view is unfinished. These are source observations, not instructions to duplicate incomplete behavior. Responsive layout, dark theme, accessible semantics and actual permissions are specified elsewhere as explicit extensions.

Evidence boundary: this focused pass is a source-level comparison. The earlier reference browser inspection is recorded in section 01. It does not establish that every authenticated production state has been visually exercised.

Contrast resolution — proposed extension: locally calculated sRGB contrast is 4.35:1 for white on clay-500, 2.88:1 for ink-400 on white, and 4.28:1 for ink-500 on paper-050. Preserve those source tokens in the reference register. For the production target, introduce action-accessible #C24720 with white text (4.98:1), keep clay-600 for hover, use ink-600 #4C5A61 for small supporting text on paper, and ink-500 or darker for meaningful metadata on white. This is a deliberate small fidelity adjustment, not an unnoticed color substitution. Final rendered pairings must be measured in all themes.

No alpha-faded body text. Decorative separators may use the source low-contrast hairlines; important unchecked-control outlines need stronger contrast. Avoid using color alone to distinguish selection, error, success, or an unread item.

04 · Typography and content rules↑ Top

Reference + Extension
Role Specification Where it appears
Display Instrument Sans 600; 48px/1.12; hero 60px/1.06; tracking −.03em Marketing hero and large statements.

Micro label JetBrains Mono 500; 11px/1.2; .09em tracking; uppercase Section keys and status labels.

Literal type scale: 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20, 24, 30, 38, 48, 60px. Prefer medium and semibold hierarchy over pervasive bold. Counts and metrics use tabular numerals. Paragraphs normally cap at 64ch; marketing support text at 36ch and hero body at 52ch. Balance headings; do not truncate primary object identity without an accessible full version.

Instrument families are substitutions explicitly supplied by the reference. They are the target families for this specification. Font files are not in the folder. Production font delivery must avoid layout jumps; use appropriate fallbacks and preserve measured wrapping. No externally hosted font is required to read this standalone specification.

  • Use sentence case for navigation, buttons, titles, and fields. Uppercase is restricted to the mono micro-label/badge role.
  • Actions name the verb and object: Create project, Save changes, Request to join, Close sprint, Restore file. Do not use vague Submit or OK.
  • System prose is plain and specific. Body sentences and hints use periods; labels and action names do not. Use no exclamation marks in system messages.
  • Metadata uses digits, a middle dot between segments, relative time under a week, and an absolute short date afterward. Provide exact timestamp and timezone where timing affects work.
  • Preserve user-entered spelling, casing, pronouns, filenames, project identifiers, and message content. Brand copy rules do not rewrite user data.
  • Translate interface labels through the existing localization path. Reserve room for longer translations; never bake text into UI images.

06A · Brand system amendment↑ Top

Decision + Reference · 23 September 2026

The NetworkBase rounded-square dot system is the approved product baseline. It is the only identity mark: alone it is the app icon; leading the name it is the wordmark; in motion it is the loading language. The generated asset kit is the canonical interim production kit until formally replaced by official supplied artwork. This amendment supersedes earlier placeholder wording and any contrary statement that places the dot after the name.

Identity and name

  • The canonical resting lockup is [dot] NetworkBase, with exact capitalization and no space between “Network” and “Base”. It is Instrument Sans semibold with tight tracking (--tracking-tight); no alternate typeface, gradient wordmark, “NB” header treatment, or improvised sparkle substitutes for it.
  • The horizontal lockup is the default. Use stacked form only in square placements, NB only where a compact monogram is specifically required, and dot-only for favicons, collapsed navigation, avatars, and any scale below the wordmark floor.
  • The dot is rounded-square, not a sharp generic square. Mark diameter, corner radius, gap, and optional protective padding derive from the wordmark’s type size. Reserve one dot-width (0.41 × type size) around the full mark. The lockup has a 14px minimum; dot-only has a 12px minimum.
  • Brand marks are transparent on ordinary product surfaces. Use a paper or ink slab only where contrast needs it; over imagery, a slab is mandatory. On an accent slab the dot inverts to the primary foreground. Never recolour beyond the accent system, stretch or squash the mark, alter its gap, place it on a busy ground, or treat the seam variant Network·Base as the standard lockup.

Colour, type, and icon boundary

  • Brand primitives are Clay #D14E24, Ink #141A1E, and Paper #FAF8F4. In themed product UI, the mark resolves through --primary, with Clay as the default accent; exported identity files stay fixed-color and must never inherit a user accent.
  • Brand colour must flow through the existing primitive → semantic → component token layers. Components consume semantic roles such as --primary, --primary-foreground, --surface-inverse, and --status-danger, never new hard-coded colour values.
  • The standalone brand icon is not a replacement for functional UI icons. Keep the Lucide vocabulary, 1.75 stroke weight, established sizes, accessible names for icon-only controls, and real third-party service logos. The dot may denote NetworkBase itself, a brand/status marker, a system avatar, or an empty state—not “search”, “settings”, “attach”, or another functional command.
  • Profile-image fallbacks remain deterministic user-initial palettes; they are distinct from the NetworkBase system avatar, which uses the dot asset. Presence remains an independent realtime state and never inherits brand semantics.

Static icon and metadata contract

  • Use the supplied Paper SVG as the canonical icon source at every size, preserving its colours, centred 32% mark, proportions, and corner geometry. Maskable icons fill the transparent corners with Paper so the operating system can apply its own mask. Do not crop, stretch, or combine the icon with the wordmark.
  • Browser tabs use icon-paper-tab.svg and matching PNG/ICO fallbacks. Inset the Paper background 8% on each side to prevent Safari from adding a black contrast outline; keep the centred orange mark at its original size and preserve both colours. Touch, installed-app, and notification icons retain the original tile.
  • Install and maintain vector favicon.svg, legacy favicon.ico, icon-paper-180.png for Apple touch, icon-paper-mono.svg for Safari pinned tabs, distinct 192/512 “any” icons, and distinct full-bleed 192/512 maskable icons. The web manifest, metadata, service-worker fallback, social preview, sign-in, legal, marketing, and application shell must all reference the same approved identity set.
  • Use Paper icon files for standard external/platform placements, installed apps, notifications, and settings. Use the Paper mark silhouette in monochrome when the target requires one colour. App tiles and favicons are fixed assets, not dynamic theme controls.

Intro and loading system

  • At splash, first authenticated paint, or sign-in landing only, the dot begins at the right edge of the future wordmark, holds, sweeps left, and reveals the name in its wake from “e” to “N”. It plays once per session. Everywhere else the resting wordmark is static. Reduced-motion users receive the resolved mark without animation.
  • The dot is the only general loading indicator. Suppress it for waits under 300ms; use breathe by default for waits below 1.5s and shuttle for expected 1.5–4s waits. turn, trace, and split are foundational alternatives; wipe, squash, queue, orbit, relay, and cast are bolder options; tally and shatter are reserved for splash/opening moments.
  • Every loading mechanic must resolve from its current motion into one still dot—no snap, dead frame, fake percentage, or generic spinner. Slow connections may slow the cycle. At 10 seconds, stop the animation and show the dot in --status-danger with a clear recovery message; mechanics requiring multiple dots fall back to breathe below 16px.
  • Loading state must be announced only when it conveys meaningful status, must not create repeated live-region noise, must preserve layout width through resolution, and must honor both prefers-reduced-motion and the saved reduced-motion preference.

Implementation and verification boundary

  • One shared wordmark primitive and one shared dot-loader primitive are required before individual routes adopt this system. Local loading skeletons may remain for content structure, but generic spinner replacements require the central loading contract.
  • Validate light/dark themes, all accent themes, 200% zoom, narrow layouts, keyboard focus, reduced motion, browser-tab/favicon rendering, PWA maskable crop, Apple touch icon, and stalled/retry states. Replacing this interim kit with final artwork requires replacing the full asset set and re-running those checks.

Profile completion Small sunken sidebar panel with 6px progress bar and one hint. Only show if a real completion model exists; otherwise omit this demo-only panel.
Overflow Menus use white surface, 8px corners, 1px border, md shadow; action rows 34px desktop. No critical action available solely on hover. Keyboard and touch users have explicit menu triggers.

Scroll ownership: global shell fills the dynamic viewport. Sidebar can scroll independently if projects exceed its available height. Normal content has one main route scroller with stable gutter; toolbar/header stick inside that scroller. Files, document editing, and messages own their pane scroll areas and use min-height: 0 semantics. Never create competing page and pane vertical scrolling. Switching tabs preserves appropriate per-view scroll; explicit navigation resets or restores according to existing route contracts.

Header compaction: in workspace tools, the project summary and team may compact after scrolling, but project name, active tab, back path, and essential state remain visible. Sticky layers may not cover focused inputs, anchor headings, dialogs, or the composer. Anchor offsets include both global and project headers.

09 · Responsive, touch, zoom, and wide-workspace rules↑ Top

Extension

The reference has a fixed 1280px root and no responsive layout media queries. Every rule in this section is a proposed extension. Use available component/container width as well as viewport width so a card in a narrow rail behaves correctly.

Width / condition Navigation and regions Content transformation
≥1440px 248px global sidebar; 56px topbar; normal content max 1200px. Discovery/project rails visible. Files may show tree, canvas, and inspector only if canvas retains at least 520px.
1024–1439px 248px sidebar retained unless user collapses it. Discover two columns only with ≥940px inner width; otherwise supporting rail stacks below feed. Tool context rails become drawers when they crowd the work.
768–1023px 56px collapsed global rail with named tooltips and expandable drawer; topbar search contracts. One main content column by default. Profile cards can use two columns when each has ≥360px. Search and form actions wrap.
<768px 56px mobile topbar with menu, compact wordmark, search, and essential notification action. Global navigation opens a drawer up to 320px or viewport−32px. 16px page gutters; single-column cards; rails accessed through labeled context buttons. Full-screen task detail/messages/file preview; sticky bottom form/composer respects safe area.
≤400px or 200% zoom Prefer text wrapping and full-width rows. Project footer becomes two rows. Tabs scroll horizontally with visible active tab. Optional metadata moves below title; primary action stays visible.
Pointer coarse 44px minimum tap targets; no hover dependency. Controls may render at 42px visually within 44px target. Do not tightly overlap target areas.
Wide board/diff Local horizontal scrolling only. Column headers remain associated with columns; compare supports unified view when two panes are too narrow. No horizontal body overflow.

Opening a drawer moves focus into it and closes the underlying mobile navigation if necessary. Back returns to the list/tree context with its selection and scroll restored. Only the topmost modal accepts focus. Persistent mobile bottom controls reserve content space equal to their height plus safe-area inset. The virtual keyboard must not conceal composer text, validation, or submit action.

Long names may wrap to two lines; metadata may wrap to a second row. Skill tags wrap; code and identifiers use controlled scroll or break opportunities appropriate to their meaning. At every breakpoint, preserve title → summary → status → action order in reading order. No absolute-positioned visual rearrangement that contradicts keyboard order.

Suggested layers: base 0, sticky content 10, global chrome 20, popover 30, drawer 40, dialog scrim 50/dialog 51, toast 60, tooltip 70. This is a proposed centralized scale; portal ownership must respect the active dialog rather than blindly using higher numbers.

Amendment (messaging rebuild, 2026-10): Messages is single pane below 1024px (list ↔ conversation; thread and details are full-screen routes with their own 56px header and Back) and split at 1024px and above (thread and details in a drawer on the same routes: 340px at 1024px, growing with the window (34vw) to 560px). This differs from "tablet untouched" for Messages only. The composer is sticky at the bottom with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), the page uses 100dvh with a visualViewport fallback, and touch inputs use 17px so iOS does not zoom. Pickers (mention, reaction, attach, project) are bottom sheets with 12px top corners and 44px rows at layer 40. Long-press (500 ms) or a 44px more button opens the message action sheet; nothing depends on hover. The floating chat launcher is layer 20 and its window layer 30; it is not mounted below 768px.

Reference + Extension
Component Visual specification State / behavior contract
Button 28/34/42px heights; 5px radius; 13px medium, 15px semibold for large. Primary clay, secondary white/border, ghost quiet, inverse white on ink, danger red. Stable width on busy label; disable duplicate action; announce busy. One dominant action per local decision region; global New project becomes secondary on workspace pages with a primary local action.
IconButton Square 28/34/42px, 16px icon centered; ghost/outline/accent/inverse skins. Required accessible label; tooltip supplements name. Selected uses aria-pressed. Touch target 44px.
Icon Lucide 1.75 stroke; currentColor; 14/16/18/24px. Decorative hidden; standalone informative icon named. Preserve third-party logos separately.
Card White, 1px default border, radius 8px, default inset 20; small 12, large 24, row container 0. Flat by default; hover border stronger only. Entire-card link must be keyboard-operable and not wrap independent actions.
Badge 20px visual height, 7px side padding, 3px radius, 11px uppercase mono; optional 5px dot. System-known status; semantic soft background and darker text. Counts do not masquerade as status.
Tag 22/26px high, 8/10px side padding, 12/13px label, pill outline. Human-chosen topic. Selected ink fill. Interactive tags are buttons with pressed state. Removal has specific name such as Remove Rust.
Avatar 20/26/34/48/72px, squared frame, deterministic fallback, source-preserving crop. Name available to assistive technology if conveying identity; repeated decorative avatar can be hidden. Availability and presence distinct.
AvatarStack 26px default, −6px overlap, max 4 in cards, +N overflow chip. Full team access available separately; stack alone is not roster navigation. Do not disclose hidden identities.
Field 13px medium label; 6px internal gaps; required indicator clay; hint/error 13px. Label associated with actual input. Hint/error IDs in describedby. Required state programmatic; error explains correction.
Input White inset well, 1px border, 5px radius, 28/34/42px; leading 16px icon and mono trailing affix. Focus clay border/wash; invalid red border and text; readonly distinct from disabled. Value survives validation and retry.
Textarea 10px×12px inset; 13/15px body; 5px radius. Forms normally 4+ lines and vertical resize; composer starts 2 lines and expands to a bounded height. Do not eat normal multiline input.
Select Input-matched native or existing accessible listbox; trailing chevron. Selected value readable, options keyboard reachable; empty/loading/unavailable choices explicit. Avoid tiny controls for long labels.
Checkbox 16px square; 3px corner; clay checked; neutral stronger outline. Real checked/mixed semantics, associated label, visible keyboard focus on drawn box, enlarged touch target.
Radio 16px circle with 8px clay center; label and optional hint. One selection per named group. Keyboard arrow behavior preserved; group purpose named.
Switch 38×22px regular or 30×18px small; white knob; clay on/paper off. Immediate-save settings only; disabled/busy and failure rollback clear. Use checkbox when a separate Save governs the value.
SidebarNav / NavItem 32px rows, 8px horizontal inset, 10px icon gap, 5px corner; 11px mono group headings. Current row paper well/clay icon, aria-current; counters mono. Route navigation uses links when appropriate.
Tabs 13px medium labels, 12px mono counts, 2px clay active underline; subtle baseline. Roving focus, arrows/Home/End, correctly linked panels. Scroll selected tab into view; no colored left-border selection.
Breadcrumbs 13px labels; mono slash; final crumb strong. At most 3 visible levels; collapse middle ancestors into accessible menu, retaining full path for nested file work.
Dialog 460px short-form baseline; 12px corner; white body; lg shadow; paper footer. Focus trap and restore; labeled title/description; Escape and dismissal follow dirty-form/critical-flow rules. Header/footer fixed, body scrolls.
Toast Up to 420px, 8px radius, 10×12px inset, 13px text; ink or semantic solid surface. Bottom-left desktop; above mobile safe area. Past-tense confirmation, optional Undo. Persistent actionable errors stay inline.
Tooltip Ink surface, 12px label, 3px corner, 4×7px inset, md shadow; no arrow. Hover and keyboard focus; do not hide essential information inside it. Correct association and collision handling.
EmptyState Dashed border, 8px corner, grid ground, 17px heading, 13px explanation max 42ch; optional 24px glyph. One relevant action only. Distinguish empty, filtered-out, forbidden, unavailable, and failed.
ProgressBar 6px track, pill ends, clay fill, 12px mono percentage. Determinate only; clamp display safely; handle max 0 without NaN. Unknown duration uses status text, not fictional percent.
ProjectCard / PersonCard See dedicated contracts. Reuse across feeds/search/profile; contextual variants share internal hierarchy.
TaskRow / FileRow No outer card duplication; 9×12px source row inset; separator at bottom. Task completion, due date, assignee; file type, provenance, size, action. Full keyboard-equivalent opening/selection.

Amendment: Slack-style messaging (2026-10)

Supersedes the three-pane layout above for /messages* (see docs/plans/messaging-slack-rebuild-report.md 7.10–7.13). The project is the workspace. On /messages* the app's own navigation stays; a 260px chat sidebar on theme surfaces sits to its right (1024px and wider), then the conversation. There is no project rail and no sidebar header: a Projects section lists every project with its unread badge; opening one collapses the list to that project's name with its channels (#general first), Add channel, Browse channels and applications below, and the name's dropdown switches projects or shows all again. The sidebar is sectioned: header with project menu, "Find a conversation" (quick switcher, also Cmd/Ctrl+K), Threads, Activity, Starred, Channels (+ Browse channels), Applications (reviewers), Direct messages (8 most recent, Show more, Invite people). Rows are the navigation row height on desktop and 44px on touch; unread rows are weight 600; counts use the neutral .nb-nav-count, the same badge as the app navigation (Report §7.11).

One conversation view for channels, DMs and group chats: 56px header (star, name 17px/600 with a one-line topic, members button, bell menu, more menu), Messages and Pins tabs, an intro block at the start of history, author-led rows grouped within 5 minutes, 12px mono day labels (sticky), one-line muted system lines, a clay "New" divider, an "N replies" line that opens the thread drawer, and a hover/focus action rail. The composer is a rich-text box (formatting shows as you type, markdown is stored) that starts two lines tall and grows to 160px; Aa toggles its formatting toolbar. Send is the one clay primary action. Browse channels, Create channel (12px dialog), the details drawer (About, Members, Pins, Settings), Activity and Threads views, and the floating launcher (400px window above a 56px button) follow the same tokens. No raw zinc, rose, blue or amber classes under src/components/messages.

Notifications tray White popover max 400px; header 17px; 34px squared avatars or 14px event glyphs; 13px event text, 12px time. Unread marker plus weight, mark read/dismiss/bundle expansion, real counts, loading, empty, failed and muted state.
Notification bundles Single compact summary row with expand chevron and mono count; children indented 12px. Keep read state and actual event grouping; do not duplicate children as additional unread counts.
Connection status Small neutral/amber status label in topbar or active surface header. Online, reconnecting, offline or unknown as actually known; message/file outbox states remain local.
Workspace indicator Compact Tasks/Requests context and counts using the global shell controls. Preserve open/close focus and current drawer state.
Confirm dialogs 460px baseline, title 20px, description 15px, 24px body inset, paper footer. Cancel and action-specific confirm; busy, failed, and dirty-exit cases; no generic OK.
Media viewer Neutral inverse canvas only when media requires it; bounded image/video, visible Close and controls. Focus contained, Escape if allowed, caption/alt/navigation, different media formats; not a glass modal.
Cookie banner/settings White 12px panel, border, restrained shadow; clear heading, body, necessary/optional choices. Keep consent categories, save/reject/accept behavior, legal links, and mobile fit. Do not rebrand away real choice information.

Toast placement is bottom-left desktop, bottom inset on mobile. Application current top-right Sonner host would be aligned later. Multiple toasts stack with 8px gap; actionable failure does not auto disappear. Menus are anchored and collision-aware; tooltips never dangle offscreen or cover primary targets.

33 · Universal state matrix and recovery presentation↑ Top

Extension

Every feature inherits this matrix. A later implementation is incomplete if it only matches the populated desktop view. The matrix specifies visual states; existing business logic decides which states are valid.

Shared skeleton shimmer contract. Content skeletons use --skeleton-base and --skeleton-highlight only, with a subtle 1.6s linear left-to-right background movement. Geometry remains local to the route, tab, card, drawer, dialog, popover, or rail it represents. With either system reduced motion or the saved reduced-motion preference, the same geometry remains visible and the movement is fully static. A region provides one polite loading announcement; individual blocks are decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Background refresh keeps loaded content in place. Pagination, uploads, saves, GitHub sync, and mutations retain their explicit status/progress controls rather than replacing content with a skeleton.
State Appearance Interaction / data rule
Initial loading Layout-matched header, card, row, rail, board, or pane skeleton using the shared neutral left-to-right shimmer. Light and dark tokens provide low contrast without accent. No empty-state CTA before data resolves. Announce loading once without repeated screen-reader chatter. Decorative skeleton blocks are hidden from assistive technology.
Background refresh Keep current content; small status near count or freshness timestamp. Do not reset selections, expanded panels, cursor, or scroll. Mark stale data when meaningful.
No content Blueprint dashed panel, small glyph, clear title, one sentence explaining next step. Show creation action only when permitted.
No matches Same quiet empty treatment; name filter/query; Clear filters action. Do not imply there are no projects/files at all.
Partial data Available regions remain; failed region has compact inline error and Retry. Unknown count is an em dash or omitted, never silently zero.
Validation Red border, text error below field, summary for long forms. Link summary to inputs; preserve values; move focus only on submit as appropriate.
Saving / sending Busy action text, stable button geometry, subtle progress indicator if known. Prevent duplicates, keep draft/outbox, report actual completion.
Success Brief past-tense toast or stable success panel for completed flows. Update the object and counts using actual returned state; Undo only if supported.
Failure Persistent local red-soft notice with correction or retry. Retry must not duplicate a previously completed action; preserve unsent/unsaved content.
Permission checking Neutral status, controls temporarily unavailable. Do not flash unauthorized actions or private data before checking completes.
Restricted / locked Allowed identity/chrome plus explanatory panel. No CSS-only masking of private content. Keep access behavior and privacy-safe wording.
Offline / reconnecting Amber or neutral status strip near active work; draft/outbox state named. No false Saved label; reconcile with existing recovery logic.
Conflict / lease Amber notice naming affected object and available resolutions. Do not overwrite changes through a purely visual redesign; preserve authoritative merge/lease workflow.
Disabled Muted control, appropriate cursor, no hover/press movement. Reason visible or discoverable without requiring activation. Disabled is distinct from read-only.
Read-only Normal readable value with quiet lock/status label; no editable affordance. Text remains selectable and links remain usable where permitted.
Selected / checked Paper well, ink-filled tag, or clay underline according to component. Semantic selected/checked/pressed attribute and visible label; distinct keyboard focus.
Hover / focus / press Border/surface darkening; clay focus ring; 1px press translation. No card lift. Keyboard focus persists regardless of hover.
Archived / deleted / expired Quiet status badge and actual available recovery action. Do not conflate soft-delete, permanent deletion, archive, or expired invitation.
Long / malformed content Wrap readable text, isolate code/path overflow, consistent fallback label. No layout collapse, XSS-prone raw rendering, inaccessible truncation, or hidden essential actions.
Session expired Inline or route-level sign-in prompt preserving return context. Respect existing draft/security behavior; do not silently discard user work.

34 · Accessibility, keyboard behavior, and input details↑ Top

Extension
  • Set a product target of accessible keyboard and assistive-technology operation, with text contrast at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text, plus distinguishable focus and important control boundaries. These are design acceptance targets; this document is not a compliance certification.
  • Use a skip-to-content link, named landmarks, one meaningful page H1, logical heading order, real links for navigation, and buttons for actions. Preserve accessible labels on compact icon actions.
  • Tabs use roving focus and arrow/Home/End keys; trees expose levels and expanded/selected state; grids/tables preserve header relationships; listbox search and selection are announced.
  • Every drawn checkbox, radio, and switch has visible focus on the visible control, not solely on an opacity-zero native input. Mixed checkboxes set the actual indeterminate state.
  • Dialogs and drawers manage initial focus, trap focus where modal, make background content inert, support context-appropriate Escape behavior, and restore focus on close. Popovers opened inside a dialog remain within its focus ownership.
  • Field labels, hints, errors, required state, units, and character counts are programmatically associated. Password reveal preserves cursor/input value. Search clear buttons name the search scope.
  • Dragging tasks, sprint items, files, columns, and social links has a keyboard/menu alternative. Drop targets use text/shape cues in addition to color. Respect permissions in both input paths.
  • Use at least 44px touch targets as the proposed product target; do not make adjacent removal/overflow actions overlap. Pointer hover is never the only path to an action.
  • Support 200% text zoom and narrow reflow. Maintain body text legibility and local overflow for code, timelines, and comparisons. Do not disable browser zoom.
  • Status color is supplemented by text, glyph, border, or pattern. Charts provide equivalent values in labels/tooltips accessible by keyboard or an adjacent table.
  • Essential save errors and conflicts remain visible; transient success is announced politely. Avoid repeated live-region announcements during typing, file progress, or realtime updates.
  • Reduced motion removes entrance delays, looping pulses, bounce, and decorative movement. The shared skeleton shimmer becomes a static neutral block. Do not use motion to convey the only completion/selection indicator.
  • Meaningful images have useful alternative text; purely decorative brand grid/icons are hidden. Preserve captions, controls, and existing accessibility support for uploaded media.
  • No user content, private identity, password, or recovery code is exposed merely to make an empty panel look populated. Accessibility enhancements do not change the underlying privacy policy.

Reference-specific repairs: clickable Card/Tag need semantics and keyboard behavior; Dialog needs focus management; Tabs need keyboard navigation and panel links; Field usage needs input associations; hidden-input focus must style visible controls; the EmptyState background shorthand must not erase its blueprint background image. Preserve the existing Radix-based capabilities rather than importing the incomplete demo behavior.

35 · Dark mode, density, and appearance preferences↑ Top

Extension

Proposed extension: the reference defines a light system and inverse marketing blocks, not a complete theme. This document specifies a coherent dark counterpart so the current application theme preference is not silently removed. Light/default is the fidelity baseline. All alternative values below require rendered contrast and asset checks.

Semantic role Light baseline Proposed dark counterpart

Card / popover / sidebar white #FFFFFF #212A30
Sunken / selected well paper-100 / paper-200 #192126 / #303C43
Default / subtle border #DBD5C8 / #E8E3D9 #53616A / #374349

Reference clay remains the wordmark color in every theme. Dark is an ink workspace, not pure black plus saturated gradients. Editors, charts, tooltips, popovers, media captions, and status chips use the same semantic mapping. Uploaded media and provider logos are not globally inverted. Theme switching must not flash the previous palette on page load.

Density Proposed spacing and dimensions Constraints
Compact Card inset 16px, panel 20px, task rows 36px, nav 32px, regular controls 32px. Do not reduce meaningful text below the reference scale; coarse pointers still get 44px targets.
Default Card 20px, panel 24px, task 40px, file 48px, nav 32px, controls 34px. Reference-derived baseline.
Comfortable Card 24px, panel 28px, task 48px, file 56px, nav 40px, controls 42px. Keep hierarchy and radius consistent; avoid changing layout families.

Accent preference decision: the existing app offers default, orchid, forest, ember, rose, and lagoon. A strict one-accent replica conflicts with that setting. Proposed behavior is to preserve the choice as an optional personal interface accent while keeping branding clay and evaluating reference fidelity in the default mode. Nondefault accent ramps must be separately specified and contrast-tested before a later implementation changes their saved values. Do not silently remove the preference or pretend alternate palettes are supplied by the reference. This remains an explicit design decision, not authorization to migrate user preferences.

36 · Reference gaps, contradictions, and proposed resolutions↑ Top

Extension
Issue Evidence Proposed resolution
No original brand assets README labels fonts/icons as substitutions and wordmark as placeholder. Use supplied identity as target direction; record placeholder status. Do not claim historical authenticity.
No mobile behavior Root fixed 1280px; app shell 820px; no layout breakpoints. Use section 09 responsive contract and macro diagrams; validate all real workflows on touch.
No full dark theme Manifest themes is empty. Use section 35 proposed semantic dark map; preserve theme setting.
Card hover conflict Written rule says border-only; Card.jsx also adds shadow-sm. Follow the written border-only hover intent; no shadow/lift on normal cards.
Primary-action conflict Prompt says one primary/view; shell and network rows show multiple. One dominant action per local decision region. Global New project becomes secondary when a workspace has a primary local action.
Rows conflict Guidance says 32px rows; actual TaskRow/FileRow size is content-driven and larger. 32px navigation; 40px tasks; 48px two-line files as proposed defaults; touch targets 44px minimum.
Weak small-text contrast Measured source pairings in section 03. Introduce clearly labeled accessible text/action aliases, retain original tokens in source register.
Mock interactions Filters, sorting, search, create, invite, file opening include simulated/no-op behavior. Retain actual application services and state transitions; reproduce appearance only.
Incomplete connections Reference Connections tab is a disclaimer empty state. Design actual connection list using PersonCard/roster patterns.
Reference stage mismatch Reference stage names differ from current project status/lifecycle models. Presentation mapping is explicit; preserve canonical data and custom lifecycle; do not invent review/paused states.
Availability vs presence Avatar prompt says collaboration availability; app tracks realtime presence. Distinct labels and contexts as in sections 06/12/27.
Emoji / imagery rule scope Reference rejects decorative emoji/photos; app supports reactions/uploads. Apply brand restrictions to authored chrome, retain user-generated content and third-party logos.
Cramped reference rails Person cards and preview footers visibly wrap awkwardly at narrow widths. Use adaptive stacked PersonCard and two-row card footer without changing core hierarchy.
Prototype accessibility Cards/tags/div dialogs/native control wrappers incomplete. Keep current accessible primitives and repair semantics/focus; do not import demo regressions.
Prototype packaging Window namespace/CDN React/runtime Babel; lint config references index.js not supplied as package entry. Use source as design evidence; define real exports/types in a later implementation only.
Missing marketing destinations Pricing/company/resource links are #; counts/prices/testimonial are invented. Only actual supported routes and verified content enter production; no new business offerings implied.
Wide tools vs page cap Reference normal content max 1200px; current files/tasks need wider canvases. Retain header/chrome pattern; allow explicit full-width tool regions, not arbitrary page-wide exceptions.
Public access assumptions Source has marketing page but current root/hub redirect to login in inspection. Document visual target separately; changing public route availability is not part of this design file.

37 · Functional preservation and design integration boundaries↑ Top

Extension
  • Preserve Next.js route identities and query contracts, including project tab, document slug, file path/node, sprint selection, analytics context, messaging conversation/reply, and workspace drawer state.
  • Preserve server authorization, public/private presentation, role-based tab visibility, masked identity, step-up authentication, and existing confirmation flows. A missing reference state does not justify weakening it.
  • Preserve React Query caching/pagination, realtime invalidation/presence, lazy feature loading, staged file startup, virtualization, and background-job progress. Visual consolidation must not load all workspaces or subscribe to all channels at once.
  • Preserve local drafts, unsaved-navigation warnings, outbox delivery, conflict resolution, collaborative document state, file leases, version history, GitHub import/sync, and IDE handoff.
  • Adapt the real shared primitives to tokens and variants in a later implementation. Do not inject the reference reset/global bundle wholesale; existing generic variable names and styling conventions may collide.
  • All feature-specific controls inherit the primitive contract. Remove one-off colors/radii/shadows during later migration only after mapping their actual semantic role; workflow and data colors may carry legitimate meaning.
  • Design-only additions in this document do not imply new endpoints, fake activity, new billing plans, expanded permissions, or backend schema changes. If a reference rail has no data source, omit or replace it with existing relevant content.
  • The source coverage register includes existing uncommitted IDE promotion/open-in-editor files. They must not be reverted or lost during any later redesign.
  • No application code, routes, database, or services were changed to produce this document. A later implementation should use this as a review map and preserve the original behavior unless the user separately changes scope.

38 · Screen review checklist and design completeness criteria↑ Top

Extension

Apply each applicable row to every route and source surface in the registers. The checklist is a future verification specification, not a report of tests already run.

Review layer Acceptance criterion Evidence expected later
Pattern assignment Every page has a named macro pattern and every exception is explained. Desktop/tablet/mobile captures with region annotations.
Reference fidelity Paper/ink/clay, typography hierarchy, 8px cards, 5px controls, underlined tabs, wordmark and square avatars match. Side-by-side reference comparison at 1280px and exact computed tokens.
Feature completeness All existing actions, fields, tabs, filters, menus, drafts and permission states remain reachable. Journey walkthrough against route/source register, including owned/member/viewer contexts.
Data truth Counts/status/time/availability match real state; no demo data substituted. Loaded, empty, partial, stale and failed cases reviewed.
Navigation Global/local navigation distinction clear; deep links and back/forward restore context. Hub→project→task/file/doc; profile/network; messages; settings paths.
Forms Required/error/hint associations, dirty/busy/success/failure behavior and keyboard flow correct. Creation 5 phases, onboarding 4 steps, auth, profile/settings, task/sprint forms.
Responsive No unwanted page horizontal overflow; narrow rails become accessible alternatives. 360/390/768/1024/1280/1440/1920px targets and 200% zoom.
Accessibility Focus, contrast, names, landmarks, keyboard alternatives and reading order work. Keyboard-only pass, screen-reader spot checks, measured text/control pairings.
Motion No spring/lift or decorative shimmer. The approved neutral content skeleton shimmer is static under reduced motion. Preference toggled across dialogs, tabs, loading, drag, chat and route transitions.
Complex tools Editors/boards keep usable space and stable scroll/selection. Large tree, large task list, long conversation, diff, upload/sync/reconnect scenarios.
Brand assets Header/auth/footer/favicons/install/social previews agree. Asset sheet and small-size/maskable previews.
Appearance Default reference mode and proposed dark/density variants stay consistent. Initial load, theme switch, saved preference, and contrast checks.
Recovery No content lost from styling changes during failure, navigation or session expiry. Draft/outbox/conflict/lease/error and retry walkthroughs.
Copy Sentence case, action-specific labels, accurate concise hints; user content untouched. Text inventory review, including loading/empty/error/legal contexts.

Recommended review order for a later authorized implementation: foundations and assets → primitives → global shell → canonical project/person cards → Discover/Network/Profile → project shell → tasks/sprints/documents/files → messages → creation/onboarding/settings → supporting/legal/error surfaces → full state and responsive review. This order is documented only; implementation has not begun.

43 · Handoff and outstanding verification↑ Top

Extension

This specification is the requested documentation artifact. It contains macro drawings, all route assignments, all component-source assignments, exact reference tokens, feature-specific appearance, interaction states, responsive adaptations, and labeled unresolved decisions. No application implementation is included.

  • Before later implementation, settle the explicit nondefault-accent preference decision, canonical project-stage presentation mapping, any replacement for the placeholder wordmark, and whether public marketing routing is meant to change. The document provides a baseline without silently changing those product contracts.
  • A full authenticated visual walkthrough remains outstanding. Verify owner, member, viewer, masked/private, offline, pending, failure, and large-data states in an authorized environment; do not treat the source register as runtime proof.
  • Reference fidelity is assessed at 1280px in light/default, then extended through the breakpoint, theme, density, and recovery matrices. Each deliberate accessibility adjustment is named rather than hidden.
  • Use the source inventory as a migration/review index, not an instruction to rewrite infrastructure. A successful redesign preserves all existing user capabilities while unifying their appearance under the supplied page patterns.

44 · Remaining gaps and readiness checklist↑ Top

Observed gaps + Design work + Verification pending

Yes: the current application still needs substantial visual integration to match the supplied page patterns. This work has produced documentation and a reference atlas only. Existing product capabilities should not be described as missing simply because they have not been restyled. The remaining work consists of observed visual mismatches, unfinished design decisions, detailed visual compositions and verification.

Rechecked against the current source on 7 September 2026. The route and component counts remain 30 and 300. The findings below do not claim a new authenticated browser audit.

What is ready, and what is not

  • Ready as a design reference: the supplied page analysis, token register, shared component contracts, feature inventory, macro page patterns, eight visual reference sections, and proposed responsive/state rules.
  • Still to complete in design: literal-spacing reconciliation, font/icon fidelity, alternate accent ramps, final lifecycle labels, detailed application-specific screens and state examples, and real-content mapping for website/rails.
  • Still to complete in the application: applying the approved design to shared foundations, shell, project/person cards, profile/project headers and all feature surfaces. No redesign implementation has been performed in this task.
  • Still to verify: the expanded atlas visually, then the implemented application with authenticated roles, complex content, responsive layouts, accessibility, themes, drafts and recovery.

Recommended order for closing the gaps

Resolve the baseline fidelity choices first. Complete shared foundations and the canonical shell/card/header designs next. Develop detailed visual compositions for each distinct workspace and form family, including representative states. Only after implementation is separately authorized should those designs be applied to the application and checked against the reference at 1280px, followed by responsive, theme, permission and recovery review.

Completion criterion: a surface is finished only when its reference pattern is identified, its actual actions/data/states have a defined presentation, the application renders that presentation, and the relevant visual and behavioural checks pass. Neither a source-register entry nor a static specimen is sufficient on its own.

Project detail amendment · 20 September 2026. The project Analytics workspace described in the historical analysis above is superseded. The implemented project detail has seven tabs: Dashboard, Docs, Updates, Sprints, Tasks, Files, and owner-only Settings. Dashboard shows one compact Recent Activity card beneath stage progress and above open roles. It shows the three latest permission-safe member joins or role updates, task moves to In Progress or Done, file additions, and completed GitHub pushes or pull requests; no charts or filters. Public visitors see only publishable events, while members see the full eligible feed. Loading, empty, error/retry, keyboard focus and both themes follow the UI-kit card system. Historical shared event tables are preserved; only the obsolete Analytics visibility key is removed by forward migration 0166. See implementation coverage for the live component ledger.
